research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and GOV.UK primary methodology only; each claim has a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, local risk score, candidate value or business result claimed

sources.name: Fuller-picture source pairing
verified_claims: ONS states that CSEW and police recorded crime together provide a fuller picture of crime experienced by individuals and households.
limitations: The sources must remain analytically separate and cannot be summed as if they counted the same events.

sources.name: CSEW preferred trend categories
verified_claims: The CSEW is better for long-term trends in violence, theft, criminal damage, fraud and computer misuse.
limitations: This preference applies nationally to covered populations and does not create local parcel estimates.

sources.name: Police-data preferred categories
verified_claims: Police data are preferred for homicide, weapon offences and robbery.
limitations: Preference for these categories does not remove recording revisions or exact-location limitations.

sources.name: Reported-crime fraction
verified_claims: ONS estimated that 36% of CSEW headline incidents excluding fraud and computer misuse were reported to police in year ending March 2026.
limitations: The national survey estimate must not be applied as a fixed reporting rate to every area or offence.

sources.name: Police-recorded violence trend caution
verified_claims: Police recorded crime is not a good indicator of trends in violence with or without injury because recording practices have changed.
limitations: Recorded violence counts must not be treated as a direct time-series measure of victimisation.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse police-data boundary
verified_claims: Police recorded data do not measure domestic-abuse prevalence and are not a good indicator of trends over time.
limitations: A police domestic-abuse count cannot be converted into a prevalence rate without an appropriate population survey.

sources.name: Sexual-offence trend boundary
verified_claims: Police recorded sexual offences are not a good trend indicator because reporting, recording and offence definitions have changed.
limitations: Recorded increases must not be interpreted solely as increased incidence.

sources.name: New sexual-victimisation questions
verified_claims: Year ending March 2026 sexual-victimisation estimates use newly developed CSEW questions and are not comparable with previously published measures.
limitations: No trend should bridge the old and new questionnaire series without a validated method.

sources.name: Stalking and harassment trend boundary
verified_claims: Police recorded stalking and harassment are not a good trend indicator because recording practices and counting rules changed.
limitations: Local changes may reflect rule or system changes rather than underlying behaviour.

sources.name: Robbery counting-rule clarification
verified_claims: An April 2025 clarification on recording robbery of business property contributed to changes in robbery and shoplifting figures.
limitations: A discontinuity around the clarification should not be treated as purely behavioural.

sources.name: Fraud system-transition omission
verified_claims: Police recorded fraud is temporarily not presented while City of London Police transitions to a new reporting system.
limitations: Missing published fraud data must not be represented as zero fraud.

sources.name: Computer-misuse transition omission
verified_claims: Police recorded computer misuse is temporarily not presented during the national reporting-system transition.
limitations: The publication gap is a data-supply limitation, not evidence of no computer misuse.

sources.name: Anti-social-behaviour question change
verified_claims: ONS states that the year ending March 2026 increase in experienced or witnessed anti-social behaviour was partly inflated by questionnaire changes from April 2025.
limitations: The survey movement must not be interpreted as entirely real-world change.

sources.name: Anti-social-behaviour recording quality
verified_claims: HMICFRS inspections found that many forces needed to improve identification and recording of anti-social behaviour.
limitations: Police-recorded ASB differences may reflect recording quality and should not be ranked as direct local risk.

sources.name: Crime-source statistical designations
verified_claims: CSEW estimates are accredited official statistics while police recorded crime and recorded fraud or computer misuse are official statistics without accreditation.
limitations: Different designations require different confidence and quality treatment.

sources.name: CSEW selected-crime scope
verified_claims: The CSEW covers selected crimes experienced in the previous 12 months, including incidents not reported to police, but excludes some populations and offences.
limitations: Survey coverage must not be described as all crime or all residents.

sources.name: Survey-estimate uncertainty
verified_claims: Because the CSEW uses a sample rather than the full population, estimates contain uncertainty and are not precise counts.
limitations: Small differences should be assessed for statistical significance before interpretation.

sources.name: Interview and incident windows
verified_claims: The year ending March 2026 estimates use interviews from April 2025 to March 2026 covering incidents occurring from April 2024 to February 2026.
limitations: The label 'year ending March 2026' does not mean every incident occurred during that exact financial year.

sources.name: Headline-crime module exclusions
verified_claims: Domestic abuse, sexual victimisation, stalking and harassment are not included in CSEW headline crime and are reported through separate modules or outputs.
limitations: Headline totals must not be described as including these separate measures.

sources.name: Police-recorded crime snapshot
verified_claims: The bulletin's police recorded crime figures are a snapshot taken on 8 June 2026 and cover data to March 2026.
limitations: Later revisions may differ, and the snapshot cannot identify exact parcel-level events.
